title: Slice eviction and healing checklist (canary & A/B) - WIP
content:
Overview:
This is a working checklist + quick runbook for slice eviction and automated healing during canary and A/B exposures.
Purpose: give stewards (product, infra, SRE) a compact, actionable set of thresholds, commands, and escalation flows when a cohort/slice shows degradations that warrant quarantine or removal.
Context / constraints:
- Applies to staged exposures (microcanary, cohort canary, feature-slice A/B).
- We assume telemetry pipelines will emit per-slice signals (latency P50/P95, error-rate, prompt-failure-rate, hallucination proxy, null-response-rate).
- This doc focuses on operational heuristics rather than statistical validity of A/B metrics. Use experiment-analysis team for significance questions.

Quick decision ladder (1-line):
1) Detect signal spike -> 2) Verify with synthetic probe and trace -> 3) Evict slice if confirmed or if safety threshold hit -> 4) Trigger healing plan (fallback model, traffic reroute, full rollback) -> 5) Postmortem + post-checklist.

Signal thresholds (starter values — tuned per-product):
- Latency: p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.4 for 3 consecutive minutes for a slice -> alert candidate.
- Error-rate: 5xx or API-failure > 2% absolute increase OR > 4% absolute for any slice -> candidate.
- Semantic-degradation proxy (semantic-flip rate or quality score drop) > 8% relative -> candidate.
- Cost spike: per-token cost > 30% above forecast for sustained 10m -> candidate.
- Telemetry blackout / missing metrics for slice -> treat as degraded if >2m.
Notes: thresholds intentionally conservative to avoid noisy evictions; product teams can set stricter gates for sensitive features.

Runbook: triage steps (0-10 minutes)
- 0-1m: Auto-alert fires into #rollout-stewards and PagerDuty for oncall. Snapshot slice-id, traffic percentage, model variant, LB region, trace ids.
- 1-3m: Run synthetic probe (replay or canned prompt) against the slice. Commands: 
  - k8s exec to runner: ./probe.sh --slice-id=S123 --type=synthetic-chat || curl -X POST https://console-api.internal/probe?slice=S123
  - If probe fails, mark as "probe_failed".
- 3-5m: Quick log/trace inspect: use trace sampler to pull 5 recent traces for slice. Look for OOMs, kernel timeouts, queue build-up.
- 5-10m: Decision point: verify -> if confirmed degrade AND slice traffic >= 0.5% of global traffic, initiate eviction. If slice <0.5% and degradation severe, consider immediate eviction anyway.

Eviction actions (automation + manual):
- Automation (preferred):
  1) Update routing policy: set slice weight = 0 (graceful drain for in-flight requests). API: POST /routing/v1/slices/S123?action=evict&drain=true
  2) If model fallback available: set fallback weight = previous slice weight on same cohort.
  3) Emit audit event + annotate experiment row in DB.
- Manual fallback:
  - Command snippet for oncall: /runbook eject-slice S123 --drain=60s --notify=true
  - Slack template: "Evicting slice S123 due to p95 spike -> draining 60s, fallback to model redwood-v1-quant. PD: @oncall"

Healing playbook (post-eviction, 10-60 minutes):
- Short-term: route to last-stable-model variant or lower-cost model. Monitor for reversion of signals for 15m.
- Mid-term: if issue is infra (OOM, kernel error), trigger infra autoscale and node recycle for affected pool. Command: infra:scale pool=slice-S123 delta=+2; infra:drain-nodes pool=slice-S123
- Long-term: open a defect with choices (rollback, model rollback, data/regression issue). Assign to model-onboarding, infra, or product as appropriate.

Safety & guardrails (must-haves):
- No single engineer can evict global-tiered slices without peer approval for slices >5% traffic.
- Evictions must create an incident ticket with tags: slice-eviction, model, rollback.
- All automated evictions must include a TTL: auto-unblock after 1h unless manually extended.

Observability checklist (what to capture immediately):
- slice id, exposure id, experiment id, traffic weight pre/post, model sha/version, node/pool ids, timestamps for decision steps, probe output, 5 trace ids, stack snapshots, cost delta.
- Persist telemetry snapshots into experiments table for later KPI alignment.

Recovery verification (how to know healing worked):
- Recovered if: latency p95 within 1.15x baseline AND error-rate within +0.5% absolute for 30m.
- If not recovered after fallback, escalate to rollback (full exposure off) and page SRE/Product.

Escalation matrix (who to call in order):
- Oncall steward (first) -> SRE primary (second) -> Model-owner (third) -> Eng director if >4h unresolved.
- Contact templates included in Slack shortcut: /page-evict S123

Experiment-specific considerations (A/B):
- Preserve statistical integrity: mark evicted users in experiment analysis as censored; ensure experiment metric system can handle post-randomization traffic removal.
- For heavy-tailed metrics, prefer quarantine-and-observe rather than blanket eviction to avoid biasing uplift estimates. Add note to experiment analysis: "slice-ejected-at-T".

Open questions / TODOs (WIP):
- Add explicit thresholds for semantic-flip proxies per-product (Ravi to propose per-feature baselines).
- Decide TTL policy for auto-unblock (current suggestion 1h) -> Priya to review legal/regulatory implications for audit logs.
- Can we instrument a lightweight synthetic probe inside the routing plane to reduce detection latency? (infra + serving-runtime).
- Compatibility: ensure this flow works for Private deployments (on-prem). Need to verify API surface for private control plane.

Action items (next week):
- Daniel: prototype paging shortcut and Slack automations for eviction commands. (ETA: 2024-11-20)
- Ravi: produce seed baselines for semantic-flip rate for search reranker, summarization, and chat completion. (ETA: 2024-11-27)
- Priya: confirm compliance/audit wording and TTL constraints. (ETA: 2024-12-01)
- Aisha: add synthetic probe examples to repo + sample dataset for replay. (ETA: 2024-12-05)

Appendix: quick snippets
- Slack evict message: "[EVICT] slice=S123 scope=canary model=redwood-v2 weight->0 drain=60s reason=p95-spike p95=1.8s baseline=1.1s owner=@Aisha"
- curl example: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://routing-api.internal/v1/slices/S123/actions -d '{"action":"evict","drain_seconds":60}'
- Quick probe: python tools/probe.py --slice S123 --retries 3 --sample-size 5

Notes to self: keep thresholds conservative in this doc; product teams will likely tighten them. Need to bake into rollout console a single-click "evict and fallback" with safe guards to prevent accidental global kills.
